title: Persistent sessions owned by a server
body:
A decade session should outlive its window and mostly survive a reboot. Today every pane is a Wayland client of the decade process, and closing the window ends decade and every program in it.

Jack's requirement, from 2026-11-07: a server owns the session and its panes, a window only views it, and the layout and each pane's cwd come back after a reboot. herdr's session model was the starting reference. Jack kept only the server-owned, persistent part of it and dropped herdr's agent detection and sidebar.

Pieces, each its own issue:

- how the server and its viewers are split, and how frames and input travel between them
- the session directory, names, and the commands that start, attach to, list and stop a session
- saving the session and restoring it at server start
- remote viewing, over the network

notes.author: Jack Roddy/575e4e76
notes.text:
Jack's design, 2026-11-07:

- One decade server holds every workspace. A workspace is a project, with its own split tree and default cwd. A viewer shows one workspace at a time and switches between them with a key or the palette.
- The viewer is built into the same decade binary as the server. Code the viewer does not need is compiled only on Linux, so the binary can be built for macOS (or another OS) as a viewer alone. Jack's only other machine is a MacBook, so remote viewing is only worth having if the viewer runs on macOS.
- decade uses its own protocol between server and viewer. No outside server protocol or client app (RDP, VNC, WebRTC and the like) is adopted. If decade cannot do it well itself, it is not done.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/575e4e76
notes.text:
Where things stand on 2026-11-08.

## Branches

- All sessions and UI work is on the `sessions` branch, which is checked out. It is not merged into `dev` and not pushed.
- Jack's launcher (`scripts/launch`, linked as `decade-dev` and `decade`) builds whatever branch is checked out. On `sessions`, `decade-dev` is the viewer, and it starts `decade server` if none answers.
- `decade stop`, `decade restart`, `decade status` and `decade list` control the server. `decade restart` saves and restores the workspaces.
- To look at the UI without Jack, run `decade script` against a server with its own `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` and `XDG_STATE_HOME` (CLAUDE.md, Running decade).
